proposed_comments.title: Skip ICU lookups when descriptions are disabled
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] Skip ICU lookups when descriptions are disabled

**Severity:** `medium`

This newly added path calls the uncached native ICU name lookup once for every code point, even when `ShowUnicodeDescription` is disabled and the toolbar hides descriptions. Guard the lookup at its call site so disabled descriptions do not incur native name lookups.

```suggestion
            string name = _settingService.ShowUnicodeDescription ? UnicodeHelper.GetCharacterName(codePointString) ?? string.Empty : string.Empty;
```

confidence.rationale: The exact source shows the unconditional description construction, the disabled-display flag, and the per-code-point native ICU call path.

### [P2] (1/2) Let the character-set dialog content shrink horizontally

**Severity:** `medium`

The new content grid fixes its width at 540 DIPs while Settings supports a 480-DIP minimum window width, before dialog chrome and margins are accounted for. Allow the grid to fit the dialog's available width; keep the paired list-height change selected as well. This is a constraint-based layout concern; clipping has not been claimed as runtime-reproduced.

```suggestion
                    <Grid MaxWidth="540" RowSpacing="8">
```

proposed_comments.title: Render standalone marks in multi-code-point descriptions
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] (2/3) Render standalone marks in multi-code-point descriptions

**Severity:** `medium`

`GetCharacterDescription` formats each code point's raw string, so a standalone combining mark appears without a base glyph in a multi-code-point description. Use the shared display transform for this display segment; retain the original code point and Unicode-name data.

```suggestion
            string.Format(
                CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
                "{0}: (U+{1:X4})",
                UnicodeHelper.GetDisplayText(info.Str),
                info.CodePoint)));
```

confidence.rationale: The added description formatter interpolates raw code-point strings; the shared helper is applied only to the displayed text.

proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] Distinguish surrogate pairs from multi-code-point strings

**Severity:** `medium`

A UTF-16 surrogate pair encodes one Unicode code point, and this method decodes both code units together. The current XML example therefore conflates UTF-16 representation with code-point count. Use a true multi-code-point example such as `°C` and describe surrogate-pair decoding separately.

```suggestion
    /// For strings containing multiple code points (e.g. combining sequences or "°C"),
```

confidence.rationale: The method documentation and ConvertToUtf32 loop directly establish the mismatch.

proposed_comments.title: Restrict the system ICU import to System32
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] Restrict the system ICU import to System32

**Severity:** `medium`

This import is documented as using the Windows system ICU library but resolves the bare `icu.dll` name without an explicit System32 search restriction. Apply the same `DefaultDllImportSearchPaths` policy used by the repository's other ICU import so resolution matches that system-library intent. This is a loader-policy hardening concern; no malicious load or runtime exploit is claimed.

```suggestion
        [DefaultDllImportSearchPaths(DllImportSearchPath.System32)]
        [DllImport("icu.dll", EntryPoint = "u_charName", CharSet = CharSet.None, CallingConvention = CallingConvention.Cdecl)]
```

confidence.rationale: The import target and repository's System32 ICU precedent are grounded; no exploit or malicious-load behavior has been reproduced.

proposed_comments.title: Show punctuation keys as glyphs and distinguish keypad divide
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] (1/2) Show punctuation keys as glyphs and distinguish keypad divide

**Severity:** `medium`

`KeyLabel` currently exposes enum identifiers such as `COMMA`, `PERIOD`, and `DIVIDE` directly in the reference guide. Map punctuation keys to their glyphs, keep slash and keypad divide distinct, and use a localized label for keypad divide. Apply the matching resource addition with this change.

```suggestion
                            kvp.Key switch
                            {
                                LetterKey.VK_PLUS => "+",
                                LetterKey.VK_COMMA => ",",
                                LetterKey.VK_PERIOD => ".",
                                LetterKey.VK_MINUS => "-",
                                LetterKey.VK_MULTIPLY_ => "*",
                                LetterKey.VK_SLASH_ => "/",
                                LetterKey.VK_DIVIDE_ => getLocalizedString(
                                    "QuickAccent_ReferenceGuide_NumpadDivide"),
                                LetterKey.VK_BACKSLASH => "\\",
                                _ => kvp.Key.ToString()
                                    .Replace("VK_", string.Empty, StringComparison.Ordinal)
                                    .TrimEnd('_'),
                            },
```

confidence.rationale: The new view model binds enum-derived labels directly and the exact mapping contains separate slash and keypad-divide keys.

### [P2] (2/2) Add the localized keypad-divide label

The reference guide needs a separate localized name for the keypad-divide key so it is not conflated with the slash key's `/` glyph. Add the resource and keep it selected with the view-model mapping.

```suggestion

  <data name="QuickAccent_ReferenceGuide_NumpadDivide" xml:space="preserve">
    <value>Numpad /</value>

```

proposed_comments.title: Allow saving an empty character-set selection
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] Allow saving an empty character-set selection

**Severity:** `medium`

Disabling Save when the count reaches zero prevents users from removing the last selected set. The setting setter persists an empty selection, and the page has an explicit no-character-sets warning for that state. Keep Save enabled so the user can commit the empty selection.

```suggestion
            CharacterSetsDialog.IsPrimaryButtonEnabled = true;
```

confidence.rationale: The dialog disables its Save action at zero selections while the bound setting setter and warning explicitly support the empty state.

proposed_comments.title: Refresh the open guide with current selections
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] Refresh selected-set data when the guide is already open

**Severity:** `medium`

When this non-modal guide already exists, reopening it with new `selectedLanguageCodes` only brings the old window forward. After changing character sets in Settings, the guide can therefore continue to show the previous “Selected sets” group. Refresh the existing view model from the supplied codes and update its filtered collection before foregrounding the window.

confidence.rationale: The entry point receives fresh codes from current settings but the existing-window branch only foregrounds a model created with prior codes.

proposed_comments.title: Remove the stale UnicodeInformation NOTICE entry
proposed_comments.body:
### Remove the stale UnicodeInformation NOTICE entry

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `Directory.Packages.props` — the removed UnicodeInformation package version; `NOTICE.md` — the NuGet package list.

**Problem:** The PR removes the UnicodeInformation package version from the central package list, but `NOTICE.md` still lists `UnicodeInformation`.

**Why it matters:** `.pipelines/verifyNoticeMdAgainstNugetPackages.ps1` treats unexpected extra NOTICE entries as errors; only Moq and MSTest are allowed extras.

**Suggested change:**
1. Remove the `- UnicodeInformation` entry from the NuGet package list in `NOTICE.md`.
2. Run the repository NOTICE/package consistency check after NuGet restore and confirm no extra package remains.

**Verification:** Run `.pipelines/verifyNoticeMdAgainstNugetPackages.ps1` with the repository's supported PowerShell and restored package metadata; confirm it exits successfully and reports no unexpected extra packages.

confidence.rationale: The changed central package version entry is removed but NOTICE still lists the package; the repository verifier rejects unapproved extra NOTICE packages.
